summary: This is a clean, well-scoped additive UI feature: client-side pivot-table and chart view modes over already-fetched report_definitions/ReportOutput results, with all grouping/aggregation math isolated in a single pure, unit-tested module (pivot-utils.ts) and zero new DB or server-side aggregation, correctly honoring the thin-client constraint. The chart color wiring (var(--color-chart-1..5) referencing the @theme inline aliases of --chart-1..5) is correct and verified against globals.css, the previously-unvalidated/missing-dark-mode chart palette was properly fixed via the dataviz skill's validator, and both `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint` ran clean in this review confirming the worker's self-reported checks. No migrations, schema, auth, permission/payment/billing/rls, .env, or .github/workflows changes are present, and no heavy-deletion pattern applies, consistent with the tier1 classification. The only notable widening is ReportFilters.tsx now letting a user attach arbitrary free-form key/value params to the report-run request instead of just projectId/companyId; this isn't a new vulnerability introduced by this diff (a client UI restriction was never a real security boundary and the same endpoint was already reachable with arbitrary params via direct fetch/devtools), but it does modestly widen the discoverable parameter surface and is worth a backend-side param-validation follow-up in the report execution service, which lives outside this repo/diff.
issues: ReportFilters.tsx lets users attach arbitrary free-form param names/values to the report-run POST body; not a new hole (the endpoint was always callable directly with arbitrary params) but worth a follow-up to confirm the backend report-execution service validates/authorizes params per-tenant rather than trusting them.

Minor UX-only quirk, not a bug: when a result has only one column (e.g. an array of primitives), PivotTable/ReportChart default both the row/category field and the value field to that same single column, producing a self-grouping pivot by default until the user changes a selector.
